details:
Project Details – Lunar Scope

Lunar Scope is an interactive lunar landing-site exploration and mission-planning platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Its main purpose is to help mission planners explore potential lunar landing locations, particularly around the challenging lunar South Pole, and understand environmental conditions that may affect future lunar missions.

What does it do and how does it work?

Lunar Scope provides an interactive 3D Moon that users can rotate, zoom, pan, explore, and interact with. Users can select potential landing locations through the globe or by entering latitude and longitude coordinates. The platform includes a mission-control interface designed to bring lunar exploration and landing-site analysis into one environment.

The planned scientific analysis capabilities include calculating Sun and Earth positions relative to a selected landing site, examining solar elevation and illumination periods, identifying terrain obstructions, evaluating Earth visibility for direct communication, and comparing different landing locations and mission dates. These capabilities are intended to help users understand when a landing site may receive sunlight and when communication with Earth may be geometrically possible.

What benefits does it have?

Lunar Scope aims to make complex lunar information easier to explore and understand through interactive 3D visualization and a centralized mission-planning interface. It can help identify potential challenges associated with limited sunlight, terrain shadows, and communication blackouts before a mission is planned. Comparing different locations and dates can also help planners evaluate alternative mission scenarios.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to support better-informed lunar landing-site selection and mission planning, especially in the lunar South Pole region, where extreme lighting conditions and complex crater terrain create significant challenges. By making environmental conditions easier to visualize and evaluate, Lunar Scope aims to contribute to safer, more efficient, and better-prepared future lunar exploration missions.

Tools, programming languages, and technologies

We developed Lunar Scope using a modern full-stack architecture:

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS.
  • 3D Visualization: Three.js, React Three Fiber and Drei.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Scientific Processing: NumPy, SciPy, Skyfield and Astropy.
  • State Management and Data Fetching: Zustand and TanStack Query.
  • Charts and Visualization: Recharts.
  • Testing: Vitest, React Testing Library, Pytest and Playwright.
  • Data Storage: Optional Supabase/PostgreSQL integration.

The project is a software-based platform, so no dedicated physical hardware is required.

How is the project creative?

The creative aspect of Lunar Scope is its combination of an interactive 3D lunar environment with a mission-planning approach. Instead of presenting lunar information as separate scientific tables or static images, the platform is designed to let users explore locations visually, select coordinates, examine environmental conditions, and compare mission scenarios in one place.

A key part of our approach is connecting the lunar surface environment with operational requirements such as solar power availability and communication opportunities. This makes the platform more than a 3D Moon viewer: it is designed to become a decision-support tool for lunar exploration.

What factors did our team consider?

Our team considered several important factors when designing the platform:

  • Solar illumination: Sun elevation, azimuth, sunlight duration and terrain shadows.
  • Communication availability: Earth position, elevation, visibility and potential terrain obstruction.
  • Terrain conditions: Lunar elevation, slopes, crater features and local horizon profiles.
  • Location accuracy: Correct lunar latitude and longitude conventions and coordinate transformations.
  • Time accuracy: Consistent UTC timestamps and scientifically appropriate ephemeris calculations.
  • Data reliability: Using trustworthy scientific sources and clearly distinguishing real, sample, and illustrative data.
  • Usability: Making complex scientific information understandable through an accessible interface and interactive 3D visualization.

Ultimately, Lunar Scope aims to bridge the gap between complex lunar scientific data and practical mission-planning decisions.
